1.title: Scenario Workshop
1.text: Welcome to Module 15: Scenario Workshop. You now know the framework. Most exam questions ask you to apply it in a situation. In this module you will learn a five-step method, and then use it on eleven worked scenarios. Every scenario is new: none of them appeared in the practice questions of the earlier modules.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Use a five-step method on any situational question. Name the owner of a decision before you read the options. Find the rule: stated, implied or absent in the Guide. Remove options by the way they go wrong, then choose the best of the rest. And solve eleven worked scenarios across roles, events, artifacts and the organization.

1.title: The Five-Step Method
1.text: Here is the method. It is the course's own, not the Guide's. Step one: read the last sentence first, because that is what is actually asked. Step two: name the role and the owner of the decision. Step three: find the rule in the Guide. Step four: remove the options that break a rule. Step five: choose the best of what remains. On the real exam you have about seventy-two seconds a question, but the method is quick once it becomes a habit.

1.title: Steps 1 and 2: Read, Then Name the Owner
1.text: Steps one and two of the course's own method. Read the last sentence first. Is it asking for the best action, for what the Guide says, or for which statement is correct? Then think of your own answer before you read the options. Next, name the owner. The Product Owner owns value and the order of the Product Backlog. The Developers own how the work is done, and the Sprint plan. The Scrum Master owns Scrum and the team's effectiveness. And watch the words best, first and most likely.

1.title: Step 3: Find the Rule
1.text: Step three: find the rule. This step goes beyond the Scrum Guide. Scrum Alliance's study guide suggests asking whether an answer is stated, implied or absent in the Guide. Stated: there is one Scrum Master on the team; accept it. Implied: only the Scrum Team attends the Retrospective; accept it if the Guide's logic leads there. Absent: use relative story points when sizing; treat it as not part of Scrum. And check an absolute word before rejecting it. Only the Product Owner cancels a Sprint is a real rule.

1.title: Steps 4 and 5: Remove, Then Choose
1.text: Steps four and five of the course's own method. Remove options that command or assign work. Remove options that give a decision to the wrong owner. Remove options that add what Scrum lacks, such as a project manager, a hardening Sprint, a Sprint zero, or an approval gate. Remove options that do nothing or wait. Then choose the one that serves, coaches or facilitates, keeps Scrum intact, leaves decisions with their owners, and acts. Let us practice.

1.title: Worked Scenario 1: A Plan Handed Down
1.text: Scenario one. Maya arrives at Sprint Planning with a finished Sprint Goal and a list of items the Developers must commit to. What should the Scrum Master do? Choose your answer. Step one: the question asks for the Scrum Master's best action. Step two: the Developers select the items, and the whole team shapes the Sprint Goal. Step three: that rule is stated. Step four: A gives the decision to the wrong owner, and B and D add a signature and a stakeholder approval. Step five: the answer is C.

1.title: Worked Scenario 2: Tasks and Reports
1.text: Scenario two. A Lakeshore Transit department manager asks the Scrum Master to assign tasks to individual Developers and to send a weekly report on each person's progress. What should the Scrum Master do? Choose your answer. The owner of who does what is the Developers. The rule is stated: the team is self-managing, and the Sprint Backlog is visible. Options B, C and D all assign tasks, which removes self-management. The answer is A: explain, and point the manager to the Sprint Backlog.

1.title: Worked Scenario 3: Two Task Lists
1.text: Scenario three. Some RideLoop Developers also receive daily task lists from their department managers, and the lists conflict with the Sprint Backlog. What should the Scrum Master do? Choose your answer. The Scrum Master serves the organization by helping it understand Scrum and removing barriers. Option A undermines self-management. Option B bypasses the Product Owner. Option C misuses cancelling, which only the Product Owner may do, and only for an obsolete Sprint Goal. The answer is D.

1.title: Worked Scenario 4: Who Builds What
1.text: Scenario four. Maya tells the Developers which person should build each item and in which order the tasks must be done. What is the best response from the Scrum Master? Choose your answer. The owner of how is the Developers, and the rule is stated: nobody else tells them how to turn items into Increments. Option A picks the wrong owner. Option C adds a manager's review. Option D waits a whole Sprint. The answer is B: coach both people.

1.title: Worked Scenario 5: A Scrum Master Who Can Test
1.text: Scenario five. The Scrum Master has strong testing skills, and the Developers ask for help with several Sprint Backlog items that are behind. What is appropriate? Choose your answer. The rule is stated: a Scrum Master who is actively working on Sprint Backlog items takes part in the Daily Scrum as a Developer. Option A uses the absolute word never, which the Guide does not support. Options B and D add steps nobody requires. The answer is C.

1.title: Worked Scenario 6: Skipping Events
1.text: Scenario six. Grace wants the team to skip the Sprint Retrospective and the Sprint Review in the coming Sprint to save time for coding. What should the Scrum Master do? Choose your answer. The Guide says that failing to operate any event as prescribed loses opportunities to inspect and adapt. Options B and D accept that loss. Option C replaces a working session with a report. The answer is A: explain, and help Grace see the value of both events.

1.title: Worked Scenario 7: An Unprepared Product Owner
1.text: Scenario seven. Maya arrives at Sprint Planning without having thought about what the Sprint should achieve, and the Product Backlog is in disorder. How can the Scrum Master best help? Choose your answer. Maya owns the order of the Product Backlog and prepares the attendees. The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by finding techniques. Options A and D take over Maya's accountability. Option C throws away the start of the Sprint. The answer is B.

1.title: Worked Scenario 8: Managers at the Daily Scrum
1.text: Scenario eight. Several Lakeshore Transit managers want to attend every RideLoop Daily Scrum to hear progress. What is the best way to meet their need? Choose your answer. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' planning event, and the Sprint Backlog is a visible, live picture of the work. Option A turns it into a status meeting. Option B adds the extra meeting Scrum tries to remove. Option C replaces planning with reporting. The answer is D.

1.title: Worked Scenario 9: A Long List of Ideas
1.text: Scenario nine. The RideLoop Retrospective has produced a long list of ideas. What should the Scrum Team do? Choose your answer. The team identifies the most helpful changes, tackles the most impactful as soon as possible, and may add them to the next Sprint Backlog. Option A is unrealistic. Option C waits too long. Option D gives the team's improvements to the wrong owner. The answer is B.

1.title: Worked Scenario 10: Slow Planning
1.text: Scenario ten. Sprint Planning takes too long because items are unclear and too large. Which practice would help most? Choose your answer. Refinement breaks items into smaller, clearer ones that are ready for selection. Option B adds an event Scrum does not have. Option C gives the selection to the wrong owner. Option D removes the plan that Sprint Planning creates. The answer is A.

1.title: Worked Scenario 11: People on Three Projects
1.text: Scenario eleven. The RideLoop Developers are each assigned to two other projects by their functional managers, and the Sprint Goals keep slipping. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? Choose your answer. People split across projects are an organizational impediment, and the Scrum Master is accountable for causing its removal, with the organization. Option A presses the team. Option B lowers quality. Option D waits. The answer is C.

1.title: Patterns Across the Scenarios
1.text: Look at what the right answers had in common. They left the decision with its owner, in scenarios one, four and seven. They helped the organization understand Scrum, in two, three, six and eight. They coached or facilitated instead of deciding, in four and seven. They kept Scrum intact, with no skipping and no extra meetings, in six, eight and ten. They made the problem visible and acted, in eleven. And they used a rule stated in the Guide, in five, nine and ten. The best answer is rarely the fastest fix. These patterns are the course's own reading of the scenarios, not Guide text.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Recap. Five steps: read, owner, rule, remove, choose. Owner first: the Product Owner, the Developers, the Scrum Master. The rule is stated, implied or absent. Remove commands, wrong owners, extras, and waiting. Choose what serves, keeps Scrum intact and acts. And for more practice, the final check in Module 18 gives you fifteen mixed questions to try under time pressure.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all eleven answers together. One: C. The Developers select, and the whole team shapes the goal. Two: A. The Developers decide who does what. Three: D. Help the managers understand self-management. Four: B. How is at the Developers' sole discretion. Five: C. A Scrum Master working on items joins as a Developer. Six: A. Skipping an event loses a chance to inspect and adapt. Seven: B. Serve the Product Owner with techniques. Eight: D. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event. Nine: B. Choose the most helpful changes, and add the top ones. Ten: A. Refinement makes items ready. Eleven: C. Work with the managers, and make the impact visible. That completes the workshop. Next, Module 16 collects the traps that recur across the modules in one place.
